messages:
olivia: Heads up — sample app in the monorepo breaks when consumed via workspace symlink in the edge runtime. Sourcemaps point to the consumer's build output instead of the original package sources. Repro steps I used:

olivia: 1) pnpm -w install
olivia: 2) cd packages/core-lib && pnpm build && cd ../../apps/sample && pnpm dev:edge

olivia: Error in runtime:

olivia: Error: Cannot find module 'core-lib/esm'
olivia:     at internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...
olivia: Repo with minimal repro: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-edge-sourcemap (private)
olivia: Anyone seen this? @mike @tara :thinking_face:

mike: Yeah seen similar. pnpm symlinks + bundler realpath logic can make `exports` paths resolve to the consumer dist. Edge bundlers (esbuild/webpack variants) sometimes inline sourcemaps that reference the symlink target instead of the package source.

mike: Quick check: what's the `exports` field in packages/core-lib/package.json? If it only has ESM entry points it can confuse older bundlers. Example we use that tends to work:

mike: ```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
```

tara: Also check that builds emit sourcemap paths without references to `../../../node_modules/.pnpm/..` etc. Our CI saw sourcemaps pointing to the workspace root which made stack traces map incorrectly in the edge env. Try `--sourceRoot`/`--mapRoot` in your bundler to force correct paths.

tara: On TS side, make sure `tsconfig` has `declarationMap` off for packages consumed as built artifacts; declaration maps can also leak local paths.

ash (ash): FWIW, edge runtimes (V8 isolates / worker envs) don't support `preserveSymlinks` node flag. If the bundler resolves via realpath it will follow the symlink and then compute sources relative to the built artifact in the consumer, not the original package. Workaround we used: either change the sample app to import from `file:../packages/core-lib/dist` (i.e., consume compiled output), or build all packages into a single output and let the edge bundler bundle that.

james: Reproduced locally — when I switch pnpm to `nodeLinker=hoisted` (`npmrc: nodeLinker=node-modules`) the issue disappears because node_modules flattening avoids symlinked path munging. Not ideal though.

ci-bot: CI failure: apps/sample-edge › startup › error: Cannot find module 'core-lib/esm' — job #142 failed (logs attached).

mike: Another data point: the edge dev server uses an esbuild plugin that expects `package.exports` to be a stable mapping. If your package.json only lists `./dist` and your src is not present in the published package, the dev server may try to resolve `core-lib/esm` via the consumer workspace structure and pick up wrong sourcemaps.

mike: Short repro I tried: create two workspaces (core-lib, sample). core-lib has `exports` -> `./dist/esm/index.js` and a `src/` folder. sample imports `core-lib/esm`. Run `pnpm -w install && pnpm -w build`. Start dev edge with `pnpm --filter sample dev:edge`. If sample hasn't consumed the built dist (only symlink), error occurs.

tara: Minimal fixes to try:
- ensure core-lib publishes `dist` that contains proper sourcemaps with `sourcesContent` or correct relative paths
- make sample import from `core-lib/dist/esm` during dev (temporary)
- set esbuild plugin `absWorkingDir` to repo root so sourcemap paths resolve correctly

olivia: Thanks — that matches our experience. For now we'll update the sample app README to recommend consuming built artifacts for edge local dev, and add a note about pnpm linker differences.

olivia: I'll file an issue for the dev server plugin to avoid resolving via realpath when package is a workspace symlink (so sourcemaps and `exports` path selection prefer package root).

mike: filing issue sounds good. tagging `eng-devex` and `eng-runtime` will help prioritize. Also add a tiny repro and CI log snippet to the issue.

ash (ash): If you want a quick patch: in `apps/sample/esbuild-plugin.js` change resolver to: `if (isWorkspaceSymlink(id)) return { path: join(workspaceRoot, packageDir, 'dist/esm/index.js') }` — ugly but works until we fix upstream.

olivia: Cool. I'll push the README change and add the issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/214 (draft).

james: FYI I also saw differing behavior between node 18/20. Node v20 with newer module resolution tends to be stricter w.r.t `exports` and fails fast. Might be worth documenting supported node versions for local edge dev.

olivia: Good call. We'll add node version note + the temporary workaround. Thanks everyone :tada:
